text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parties will either try to hide, or give a different interpretation to differences between them in order to cooperate in next year'S presidential elections.
- U.S. presidential envoy on the Cyprus dispute Richard Holbrooke plans to get active on Cyprus after the presidential elections in early 1998.
- Communist Akel party chief Demetris Christofias says he cannot foresee a solution to the Cyprus problem before the presidential elections in 1998.
- Thousands of people flocked to the beaches over the weekend as a heatwave gripped capital Nicosia with temperatures knocking on 40 degrees.

- Britain and the United Nations are working on a comprehensive solution to the Cyprus problem which will include constitutional aspects and security aspects of a settlement in a federated Cypriot state.
- State prosecutors have difficulty in supporting a case against three brothers held on suspicion of attempted murder and conspiracy to kill a gambling club owner in Larnaca last month.
- Police tighten security around people in Limassol amid concern of a new crime wave.
- The National Council, the advisory body on the Cyprus problem, meets today to discuss the forthcoming talks between the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders in New York next month.
